overview.title: Getting started
overview.body:
Copy a bundled preset, edit the user copy, validate it, and save it. Activate the saved revision only when you want the running driver to use it.

Named functions are the tool-ring entries. Direct center/rotation actions can also be used without a named tool ring. The geometry describes touchpad coordinates, not the size of the floating window.

Editing, previews, and this help never execute layout commands. Activation can make the driver execute commands and value queries. Review imported presets before activating them.

library.title: Preset library and file operations
library.body:
Built-in presets are protected: use Copy to create an editable user preset. New creates a draft; Import loads a reviewed JSON or statically readable Python layout; Export writes a portable JSON copy. Refresh rereads the library.

Renaming or deleting an active preset requires the same driver instance to acknowledge a replacement revision first. The original file remains until then. Canceling a pending operation retains the original, but does not undo a replacement request already written to configuration.

identity.title: Identifiers and display names
identity.body:
A preset identifier selects a file and must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*. It is not a path. The optional display name is only a label and never changes file selection.

Function identities and display titles are also separate. Rename changes a function identity and its references; Display title changes only the label shown to the user. Changing the interface language never translates stored names, commands, or paths.

state.title: Draft, saved, requested, applied, and recovery state
state.body:
Draft is the in-memory edit; saved is the file revision; requested is the configured selection; applied is what the running driver acknowledged. A successful save or activation request is not proof that the driver applied it.

Hot reload waits for a complete no-contact boundary. A held gesture finishes with its original snapshot. Recovery is current only after the applied revision is durably recorded. Offline status cannot confirm activation.

rules.title: Application matching and rule order
rules.body:
Application keys match the executable path before the window title, using lowercase substring matching in stored order. A compositor class/app_id is not a separate matching field.

The reserved none rule is the fallback. An explicitly empty matched rule intentionally disables bindings for that application. Move up/down changes precedence; place more specific matches before broad ones.

functions.title: Named functions and the tool ring
functions.body:
Named functions become tool-ring entries in stored order, clockwise from the top. Add, rename, remove, or reorder them here; edit their title/icon and command in the metadata dialog.

center, clockwise, and counterclockwise are reserved action regions, not function names. Switching editor views does not delete direct actions or named functions.

Preview uses the live overlay renderer with static base icons and slices_minimum_count padding. It does not execute commands or queries, guess conditional icons, or simulate live gesture values. The neutral preview background differs from the transparent desktop overlay.

actions.title: Actions and alternative order
actions.body:
Select center, clockwise, or counterclockwise, then add or edit an action. Alternatives retain their order, but modifier-specific alternatives take precedence over unmodified alternatives.

An action can emit keys, relative-axis events, run a shell command, or only control selection. A function may be command-only; no dummy key binding is required. Removing an action changes only the selected alternative.

action_type.title: Choosing an action type
action_type.body:
Keyboard combination emits the selected ordered key/button events. Relative-axis events emit signed numeric values such as REL_WHEEL. Shell command runs a command in the driver. Control / selection only performs no key or shell output.

Changing type does not automatically discard incompatible event rows. Review them before accepting; validation reports incompatible combinations. Keyboard actions may also include a command.

events.title: Event names, combinations, and relative values
events.body:
Search the catalog by event name, such as volume or ctrl. Add selected events and order them as the desired combination. Event identifiers such as KEY_LEFTCTRL and REL_WHEEL are stored unchanged.

Relative values are signed integers, not percentages or display-value queries. When combining REL_WHEEL and REL_WHEEL_HI_RES, specify each event's intended numeric value. Removing/reordering rows preserves the remaining event/value pairs.

modifier.title: Required modifier
modifier.body:
An optional modifier such as KEY_LEFTSHIFT makes this alternative eligible only while that key is held. It is a condition, not another emitted key.

Leave it empty for an unmodified alternative. Modifier-specific alternatives take precedence. Use the exact catalog event name; the interface does not translate it or infer keyboard-language characters.

trigger.title: Action trigger
trigger.body:
release runs when the gesture is released after its conditions are met. immediate runs when its gesture conditions become eligible, without waiting for release.

The selector may show translated labels, but the stored values remain release and immediate. Rotation thresholds and minimum hold duration still apply where relevant.

duration.title: Minimum hold duration
duration.body:
Duration is a nonnegative number of seconds the gesture must satisfy before the action is eligible. It is not a delay inserted after a shortcut.

Zero requires no additional hold time. Review trigger and rotation threshold together when choosing gesture timing.

command.title: Shell commands and trust
command.body:
This is executable shell text, not a label. The driver executes it as the current user when the action or named function is triggered. A keyboard action can also include a command.

The editor and help do not execute it. Do not activate an untrusted imported command merely to preview a layout; activation can also start display queries.

title.title: Display title
title.body:
A display title labels a function or action without renaming its identity or changing its output. A named function normally falls back to its identity when no title is set.

Long tool labels wrap and then use an ellipsis. The full supplied titles are available in the canvas tooltip. User-authored titles are never translated with the interface.

icon.title: Icon file or theme name
icon.body:
Use a local image path (for example, an SVG) or an installed icon-theme name. Prefer an absolute path when using a file; a relative path depends on the process working directory.

Missing or unreadable icons fall back to the display title. Import/export does not copy icon assets, and an absolute icon path from another desktop may not exist here. The preview resolves base icons locally without running a query.

unit.title: Displayed unit
unit.body:
Unit is text appended to the displayed value, such as % or dB. It does not convert the value or change emitted relative events.

The static preview does not run the display-value query, so it does not invent a value to show beside the unit.

value.title: Display-value query
value.body:
A display-value query is shell text whose output the driver reads for feedback. It can run during activation or metadata refresh, not only after an output action. Review it as executable code.

Static editing and previews never evaluate it. Relative-axis actions instead use numeric event values; their display-query field is disabled to avoid mixing the two meanings of value.

threshold.title: Rotation threshold (treshold)
threshold.body:
Enable Override to set a positive rotation threshold in degrees for this entry. Without an override, the existing driver/default threshold applies.

The historical configuration spelling treshold is intentional and is preserved in saved layouts. This is a gesture threshold, not the diameter of the rendered ring.

conditional_icons.title: Conditional icon mapping
conditional_icons.body:
Map an exact display-query result to an icon file or theme name. Query-result keys must be unique. These are result strings, not shell commands themselves.

Only the driver evaluates the query and chooses a conditional icon. The static preview shows the base icon or text fallback instead of guessing the result. Removing a row removes only that result mapping.

geometry.title: Touchpad geometry
geometry.body:
Coordinates and diameters are absolute touchpad units, not screen pixels. The driver-reported device bounds allow validation; without them the canvas is schematic, not calibrated.

Drag the circle interior to move it and the square handles to resize the outer circle, center button, or top-right activation region. The activation region stays anchored at the top right. These controls do not resize the floating overlay.

raw_json.title: Raw JSON draft
raw_json.body:
Raw JSON is a separate draft. Apply JSON to forms validates it before replacing structured values; invalid text is retained. Discard raw draft restores the last valid form representation.

While an unapplied raw draft exists, structured editing is blocked to avoid overwriting it. Save cannot silently ignore invalid raw text. JSON fields and event identifiers remain unchanged by interface translation.

save_activate.title: Save, reload, and activate
save_activate.body:
Validate checks the current document without executing it. Save writes the preset but does not change the selected layout identifier; saving an active file requests a safe reload. Activate saved revision requests that exact saved revision and waits for runtime acknowledgment.

Reload file discards local edits only after confirmation. External changes are not silently overwritten: reload them or save a separate copy. Closing the manager leaves the driver running.

trust.title: Trusted Python conversion
trust.body:
Ordinary Python-layout import uses static parsing and never executes the file. Unsupported dynamic Python is rejected rather than guessed.

Trust Python and convert is an explicit execution boundary: it runs the reviewed Python as your user. Side effects cannot be rolled back by the editor. This permission does not authorize the driver to execute other dynamic Python layouts, and offline conversion does not offer this execution path.

language.title: Interface language
language.body:
System default uses Simplified Chinese for Chinese locales except Traditional Chinese regions/scripts, Traditional Chinese for zh_TW/zh_HK/zh_MO or Hant, and English for other languages. You can explicitly choose any supported interface language.

The preference is stored in the per-user manager settings, not dialpad_dev or the preset. It takes effect the next time the manager starts; changing it never rebuilds an open window or discards drafts. User data, command text, paths, and backend error details retain their original text.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting and verification limits
troubleshooting.body:
If editing controls are disabled, check whether the preset is bundled/read-only, a raw draft is unapplied, or a rename/deletion is pending. Copy a built-in before editing. Offline mode allows editing but cannot activate or confirm a running revision.

A saved/requested revision is not an applied acknowledgment. Check the instance/revision status and driver logs when activation is pending or rejected. Missing icons may belong to a desktop theme not installed here.

Real login startup, suspend/resume, Nix builds, other desktop sessions/platforms, physical tool selection after rendering changes, and live value/conditional-icon feedback require separate acceptance. See docs/issue-31-layout-manager-plan.md for the evidence and outstanding checklist.

{path}
